items.title: QSA decode attention: PR #540's two-cells-per-step chunk kernel on every CUDA card and a bounded merge (STRATA_ATTN_DAILY=1, opt-in, bit-exact)
items.body:
## Title
Issue: none (an opt-in speed change, bit-exact).

## Summary
`STRATA_ATTN_DAILY=1` (opt-in, off by default) runs the QSA layers' decode attention - the verify window's and the MTP
drafter's, single query and batch - through PR #540's chunk kernel (`attn_chunk_kernel_pre75`: two cells per step
with a 12-shuffle reduction, cell-major probabilities, V loaded four at a time) on **every** CUDA card, and merges the
chunks with `attn_merge_v2_kernel`, a merge that skips the chunks the chunk kernel marked empty. Upstream compiles the
pre75 kernel only with `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60` and picks it below sm_75; here it is compiled in every CUDA build
and selected by the variable. The output is **bit for bit** the default kernels' (see below). HIP is untouched.

## Why
The default `attn_chunk_kernel` reduces each cell with 5 `warp_sum` shuffles per head (60 per cell pair); the pre75
body does two cells per step with `reduce12` (16 shuffles) and reads the V rows four at a time. nsys on an RTX 3060
(stage 0 of a layer split, 131K context): `attn_chunk_kernel` **99.8 us** a call against **46.4 us** with the pre75
body; the same ratio on an RTX 2080 Ti. The decode attention is ~8% of the per-row cost of a window at 131K on these
cards, so the end-to-end gain is small but free.

## What changed
- `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_decode_attn.cu`: `attn_chunk_kernel_pre75<M, NC, ...>` compiled in every CUDA build;
  `daily_attn()` reads `STRATA_ATTN_DAILY`; the kernel choice `STRATA_ATTN_CHUNK_SEL(M, PRE)` takes it on any card
  when set (below sm_75 in an experimental build as before). `attn_merge_v2_kernel` with the chunk-empty marks;
  `STRATA_ATTN_MERGE_V2=0|1` forces the merge alone, `STRATA_ATTN_PRE75=0` turns the chunk kernel off (A/B).
  `spt` shares `sq`'s shared memory, so the kernel uses 15,872 B like the default one (68-78 registers against 37-41,
  256 threads a block).
- `include/strata/kernels/qsa_decode_attn.hpp`: the selection helpers.
- `src/kernels/qsa_merge_daily_parity.cpp` (tests): memcmp of the chunk kernel and the merge against upstream's on
  four KV formats, widths at the chunk borders and non-resident pages; `--bench` times the two chunk kernels back to
  back. Registered as ctest `qsa_merge_daily_parity_default` and `_daily`.
- `CMakeLists.txt`: the harness.

## Bit for bit
`reduce12` adds at every level the same two pairs as `warp_sum`'s butterfly (xor 16, 8, 4, 2, 1; float addition
commutes), the V cells fold in the same cell order with the same `fmaf`, the masked cells stay excluded; the merge v2
does the same `fmaf` in the same order and skips exactly the chunks the chunk kernel marks empty. `qsa_merge_daily_parity` on an RTX 2080 Ti (v0.1.43 build, tests on): **1,168 cases, 0 differ** (fp16 290, int8 291, q4_0 294, k8v4 293; 21,190,308 nonzero output values), with `STRATA_ATTN_DAILY` unset and `=1`. In the engine the greedy text and the drafter's acceptance are unchanged (deterministic
131K bench, forced tokens and windows).

## Measurements
RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75) + RTX 3060 12 GB (sm_86), Windows 11, CUDA 12.6, layer split, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS,
131K context, `--kv int8`.

`qsa_merge_daily_parity --bench` on the RTX 2080 Ti (CUDA events, 200 calls per arm, B-A-B: Daily kernel, upstream
kernel, Daily kernel again; int8 KV, 32,768-cell capacity, window of n_q queries):

| n_q | width (cells) | chunk kernel: upstream | PR #540 body | ratio | merge: upstream | merge v2 | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 32,768 | 448.9 us | **264.3 us** | 0.59 | 182.6 us | **45.6 us** | 0.25 |
| 2 | 32,768 | 849.8 | **483.9** | 0.57 | 186.6 | **60.9** | 0.33 |
| 3 | 32,768 | 1,259.8 | **727.3** | 0.58 | 202.3 | **85.1** | 0.42 |
| 4 | 32,768 | 1,692.3 | **969.0** | 0.57 | 208.4 | **106.5** | 0.51 |
| 4 | 2,051 | 132.7 | **86.6** | 0.65 | 41.3 | **9.9** | 0.24 |

fp16, q4_0 and k8v4 KV show the same ratios (0.57-0.63 for the chunk kernel, 0.24-0.51 for the merge). In the engine
(nsys, RTX 3060, 131K context) `attn_chunk_kernel` went from 99.8 us to 46.4 us a call.

End to end it is part of a stack that matches its reference within noise; the attention alone is ~8% of the per-row
cost, so no separate end-to-end claim is made here.

Built and started on v0.1.43 with `STRATA_ATTN_DAILY=1` (RTX 2080 Ti + RTX 3060 layer split, Windows): the engine serves as before, same answer.

## Risks / limits
Opt-in: nothing changes with the variable unset. The kernel body is PR #540's (sskver) and the merge is Hardin22's
`attn_merge_v2_kernel`, both carried in this fork since 0.1.40 and credited in the source. #1888 (split attention on
the int8 mma path, sm_80+) is a different kernel and not bit-exact; the two do not overlap (this one serves Turing).

Part of a series from a public patch registry (`stack/` in the fork imanu86/Strata-2080Ti).

items.title: QSA decode: the window's block scores with the queries in registers and six shuffles per block (STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1, opt-in, bit-exact)
items.body:
## Title
Issue: none (an opt-in speed change).

## Summary
`STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1` (opt-in, off by default) computes the verify window's QSA **block scores** (decode, up to 4 queries)
with a kernel that keeps the queries' slices in registers and reduces the four heads with six shuffles per block instead
of twenty. Scores and top-k ids are **bit for bit** the multi kernel's (`qsa_rows_bench --rows`, `memcmp`, 16 cases per
card). CUDA only; the prompt path (#1825's territory) and HIP are not touched.

## Why
In a 131k decode the QSA kernel that grows most with the window's rows is `block_scores_multi_kernel`: ~20 us more per
call for every row of the window on both an RTX 2080 Ti and an RTX 3060 (nsys, 8 QSA layers on the second card of a
layer split). The keys are already read once for all the queries; the cost per row is in the shared-memory and
shuffle pipes - per (key block, query) 4 x `LDS.128` of the query slices and 5 shuffles per head (20 per block and
query), at 32,769 blocks ~15-20 us of issue per query.

## What changed
- `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`: `block_scores_rows_kernel<NQ>` (NQ = 1..4): the NQ queries' slices (4 heads x 4
  floats per lane) in registers for the whole kernel (44 / 63 / 78 / 94 registers, no stack); the four heads' lane
  products reduced with a scatter that keeps `warp_sum`'s pairings (xor 16 and 8 leave one head per lane, then 4, 2, 1)
  and gathered on lane 0 in head order. Tail block and the `+1e9` as before. `qsa_block_scores` takes it for the
  calls without `active_blocks` with up to 4 queries when `STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1`; otherwise, or beyond 4 queries, the
  multi kernel runs as before.
- `include/strata/kernels/qsa_select.hpp`: the `rows` entry.
- `src/kernels/qsa_rows_bench.cpp` (`EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL`): what the T rows of a verification window cost in a QSA layer's
  decode kernels at a long context (block scores, top-k, attention over each row's selection, indexer append;
  synthetic data at the real geometry, int8 pools, no model); `--rows` runs the new kernel against the multi kernel,
  scores and top-k ids bit for bit at T = 1..4 at 131k and at a short context with a full tail block, and prints both
  kernels' microseconds.
- `docs/QSAROWS.md`.

## Bit for bit
Every addition in the new reduction adds the same two operands of the same `warp_sum` level (float addition commutes),
the product expression is the same text in the same file, the relus are summed in head order. `qsa_rows_bench --rows`:
8 cases per card (T 1-4 x two contexts), 0 differ, on sm_75 and sm_86. In the engine the greedy text and the drafter's
acceptance are unchanged.

## Measurements
Hardware: RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75) + RTX 3060 12 GB (sm_86), Windows 11, CUDA 12.6, layer split, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
IQ3_XXS pack, 131k context, `--max-context 262144 --kv int8`.

`qsa_block_scores`, us per call at 131k (both kernels read the same pooled keys):

| | T=1 | T=2 | T=3 | T=4 | per row |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 2080 Ti, multi (reference) | 47.2 | 56.9 | 78.2 | 101.2 | +18.0 |
| RTX 2080 Ti, `STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1` | **36.2** | **38.0** | **49.2** | **54.6** | **+6.1** |
| RTX 3060, multi | 73.4 | 109.4 | 151.9 | 193.5 | +40.0 |
| RTX 3060, `STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1` | **63.3** | **75.5** | **98.0** | **130.2** | **+22.3** |

In the engine (nsys): per window the second card saves 0.09 ms at T=1 and 0.37 ms at T=4 (8 QSA layers), the first
0.04 / 0.25 ms (4 layers). End to end, deterministic 131k bench (forced tokens and window sizes, 1024 decode tokens,
three interleaved runs lever on / off / on): **+3.2% and +0.1%** decode tokens/s in the two B arms, text identical.
Together with the companion experts lever (`STRATA_EXPDEC=1`, separate PR): +2.9%.

Ported and validated on v0.1.43 (micro-bench bit-exact on both cards; our full stack on 0.1.43 matches our 0.1.42
daily on the forced 131k bench).

## Risks / limits
- Off by default; `STRATA_QSA_ROWS` must be exactly `1`. Only the decode calls with <= 4 queries and no `active_blocks`
  change; everything else runs the kernels it ran before.
- On the RTX 3060 at T=4 the kernel is at 94 registers (2 CTAs per SM); a two-pass version of 2 queries would stay at 63
  if that card matters more.
- Not measured on sm_80/89/120 or HIP.



**Scope.** The gain comes from VRAM-resident routed experts / decode QSA scores on Turing/Ampere setups where these kernels are a large share of the verify window. On rigs where most routed experts are off-GPU (e.g. 4x RTX 5080 16 GB, see the test in #2058) the window is dominated by stage hand-offs and host experts, and the levers measure neutral.

items.title: --batch-mtp: the first slot admission ends the engine ("unsupported native MMVQ GGML type")
items.body:
**Problem.** With `--batch-mtp`, the engine exits at the first request that goes into a batch slot:

```
strata batch: MTP admission for slot 0 failed: mtp: unsupported native MMVQ GGML type
```

The slot drafters share the main drafter's weights and draft head (`MtpDrafter::bind(..., shared)`). `bind()` copies the draft head subset (`dhead_`, `dvocab_`, `n_dvocab_`) but not its ggml type. `dhead_type_` stays -1, and `native_mmvq` refuses it. This hits every `--batch-mtp` run that has a draft vocabulary, which is the default.

**Fix.** One commit in `src/core/mtp.cpp`:

- `bind()` with a shared drafter also copies `dhead_type_`.
- `load()` with shared weights also takes the `--mtp-q4` Q4_0 copies (`dense4_`, `q4_off_`, `q4_`, `q4_head_`). They would be missing in the same way.
- `dense4_` is freed only by the drafter that owns the weights.

**Checked.** Setup: 1× TITAN RTX (Turing), UD-Q4_K_XL with the BF16 PLE table, `--batch 4 --batch-mtp --spec 4`, MTP runtime with draft vocabulary.

- Before the fix: the engine exits at the first `BGEN`.
- After the fix: `tools/batch_test.py --batch 4 --n 4 --max-new 96 --mt-min 1 --extra "--batch-mtp --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000"` reports all 4 slots IDENTICAL to their solo tokens.

Side note from the same machine: I also tried `--batch-mtp` on a 2-GPU layer split, without `--batch-groups`. It works and gives tokens identical to solo, but it needs two more changes, and on Turing it was slower than the pipelined batch without MTP. So it is not part of this PR. I can open it separately if it is of interest.

Written by my agent, tested on my machine.

items.title: V100 (sm_70): the compute-capability floor drops from 7.5 to 7.0
items.body:
The three places the 7.5 floor was written down all go to 7.0, and the messages now name the card the check begins with instead of the one it used to exclude:

* CMakeLists.txt - configure time.  `_base` is stripped of its -real/-virtual suffix first, so 70 and 70-virtual both pass; STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60 still admits a Pascal build below it.
* src/core/device.cu - run time.  This is the gate that matters even for a locally built binary: a binary carrying sm_70 code can be carried to a Pascal machine and would otherwise silently take whatever path the driver chose.
* setup.py - gpu_problem(), plus the hint in check_gpus() and the "none of your GPUs" message.  Without this the installer reports the V100 as unsupported and never reaches the compile step, so the other two gates would be invisible.

A fourth place the floor is written down is engine/BUILD.json, which is not edited: build_engine() and the HIP builder both write it, and the prebuilt carries its own copy.  Until the release tooling (tools/make_release.py, absent from this tree) emits an sm_70 asset, a V100 gets the compile-locally path - get_prebuilt() sees no code for arch 70 and falls through to build_engine(), which compiles for gpu["arch"].  The same shape as the unsupported-GPU model in docs/AMD_HIP.md.

No kernel changes.  The sm_80 guards were written for the experimental sm_75 build and key off cc_major < 8 or __CUDA_ARCH__ < 800, which sm_70 satisfies: qsa_block_scores_tc and qsa_prompt_attn_batch both refuse a V100 and prefill runs the old warp and decode kernels, and fused_gr sizes its chunk from cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin, which a V100 answers with 96 KB - more than the 64 KB the Turing comment already anticipated.  Only Volta's missing cp.async and TF32 mma cost anything, so the risk is performance rather than correctness.

docs/NVIDIA_V100.md: the gate-by-gate walk, which translation units actually use sm_80 instructions (and that native_qsa_score has no caller outside its HIP test), the Volta/Turing/Ampere comparison, and the open points - the cc_major < 8 guards are coarse enough that an eventual Turing tensor-core path needs a finer split, and the V100's doubled resident warps per SM mean the fallback kernels' register and shared-memory pressure should be measured rather than assumed.

items.title: qsa_select: coalesced streaming top-k for long Turing prompts (+23% 248K prefill)
items.body:
## What

The register top-k holds at most `TK_T * TK_PER` blocks (~135K cells). Past that the prompt path falls back to
`block_topk_kernel`, whose per-thread runs read the scores uncoalesced: 12.8 ms per 256 queries at 250K on an RTX
2080 Ti, the largest prefill phase there at that length.

`block_topk_stream_kernel` reads the keys from memory on every radix pass with block `t + i * TK_T` (coalesced), so
it has no register limit, then emits the cells in ascending chunks of `TK_T` blocks with two block scans (ties to the
lowest index), giving `block_topk_kernel`'s ids.

It is taken only where the active bound is already used (Turing prefill, or `STRATA_TOPK_ACTIVE_ANY=1` in tests) above
22,528 blocks (~90K cells). Decode and other cards are unchanged. `STRATA_TOPK_STREAM=0` keeps the previous dispatch.

`qsa_topk_active_parity` gains cases either side of the 22,528-block bound, heavily tied scores at 200K and all-zero
scores at 262K (20 cases), comparing against the capacity-dispatch reference.

## Measured

RTX 2080 Ti, 256 queries, capacity 262144, top-k with the active bound (`STRATA_TOPK_STREAM=0` / unset):

| context | before | stream |
|---|---|---|
| 90K | 0.49 ms | 0.48 ms |
| 131K | 1.03 ms | 0.75 ms |
| 250K | 12.8 ms | 1.13 ms |

Selections identical to the reference kernel 256/256 at each length. `qsa_topk_active_parity`: PASS (20 cases, ids
bitwise identical), with the stream on and off.

End to end, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, same build A/B, prefill tok/s: 248K 951 -> 1167 (+23%), 155K 1166 -> 1210 (+4%),
128K and below unchanged. `qsa select` at 248K: 70.9 s -> 22.2 s. (These runs had #742's scorer on as well.)

Only tested on sm_75. Independent of #741 and #742 (merges cleanly with both).

Developed with an AI coding assistant; all numbers measured on an RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB / i5-12490F / 64 GB.

items.title: setup: Volta (V100, sm_70) and Turing as an experimental build path
items.body:
Lets setup install Strata on a compute capability 7.x card (Tesla V100, RTX 20) instead of refusing it. The engine's kernels already have pre-sm_80 paths behind `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM75`; this makes setup use them.

## Changes (`setup.py`)
- **GPU check:** 7.x cards are accepted (below 7.0 is still refused), with a warning that this is experimental and the engine is compiled locally. The ready-made engine has no sm_70/75 code, so the existing "compiling instead" path takes over.
- **Build flag:** `-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM75=ON` is passed when any chosen card is below sm_80.
- **CUDA toolkit:** CUDA 13 dropped Volta. With an sm_70 card, `find_nvcc` picks the newest 12.x toolkit even if a 13.x is also installed, and the automatic install gets 12.9 instead of 13.0.
- **Host compiler (Linux):** CUDA 12.x refuses a distribution's current GCC (for example CUDA 12.4 with GCC 15). When the default `g++` is newer than the toolkit accepts, setup uses the newest `gcc-N`/`g++-N` it does accept for **C, C++ and nvcc together**. Setting only `CMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER` isn't enough: nvcc adds its GCC's library folder to the link line, so C++ objects built by GCC 15 then fail to link against GCC 12's libstdc++ (`undefined reference to ...basic_string::_M_replace_cold`). An existing `CUDAHOSTCXX` is left alone.

`README.md` gets a short note in "You need".

## Tested
Tesla V100-PCIE-16GB, driver 580.178, CUDA 12.4, Ubuntu with GCC 15 as the default and GCC 12 installed:
- engine 0.1.22 (this branch's `main`) builds for sm_70 through `build_engine`;
- it serves Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ2_XS: correct answers, MTP drafts accepted, about 17-24 tok/s decode on short prompts;
- a P100 (sm_60) in the same machine is still reported as not supported.

Not tested: Turing, Windows, the automatic CUDA 12.9 install.

items.title: prefill: use active QSA top-k bounds on Turing with large KV capacity
items.body:
With `--max-context 262144`, QSA score rows have a stride of 65538 blocks. A prefill batch at 131K actual context fits the register top-k kernel's 33792-block limit, but CUDA dispatch currently tests the allocated capacity and selects the reference kernel.

This enables the already supplied `active_blocks` bound **only on sm_75**. It keeps the score-row stride, selection arithmetic and kernel bodies unchanged. Other CUDA architectures retain the capacity rule, including the RTX 5070 case documented in the current source as a 1–3% regression. HIP retains its existing policy. Decode omits the bound, so captured graphs keep the capacity rule as their context grows. Invalid bounds and contexts beyond the register limit fall back to the existing dispatch. Presence of `STRATA_TOPK_CAPACITY_GUARD` restores the CUDA capacity rule for A/B runs.

The change reuses upstream's existing API and prefill caller rather than importing the separate API from our 0.1.31 fork. A CUDA parity target covers 16 cases with stride 65538: partial tails, zero/tied scores, batch sizes 1/8/255/256/257, invalid bounds, and both sides of the 33792-block limit.

### Retained measurements on our previous daily

Modified RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB, Ryzen 7 5800X, 96 GB RAM, Windows, CUDA 12.6, IQ3_XXS, KV262144/int8/resident32768, automatic elastic expert cache and MTP. Same-executable capacity/active/capacity A/B/A, two 1024-token outputs per arm; fresh prompt131248, second prompt131239 with131072 reused.

items.body:
**Don't pursue: BF16 decode GEMV via Turing tensor cores (sm_75) — measured negative**

Question: the QSA prompt attention rides the Turing tensor cores (#270-style `mma.sync.m16n8k8`); can the decode GEMVs (`bf16_gemv.cu`) do the same?

This PR adds an isolated benchmark comparing the production warp kernel against the tensor-core path on the real decode shapes (n_in = 2560, BF16 weights), with three TC variants covering the conversion cost from every angle (W preconverted once / in-register / fused no-reduce form) and a full k-split occupancy sweep for the TC side. No inference-path changes.

**Result: the TC variant loses on every real shape, 1.3–2.2×, even at its best config** — after conversion overhead:

| Shape | Baseline µs | Best TC µs | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ssm_alpha/beta [2560,48] | 8.73 | 11.32 | 0.77× |
| indexer.k_proj [2560,128] | 7.14 | 12.09 | 0.59× |
| q_proj/router [2560,512] | 9.48 | 15.78 | 0.60× |
| ple_value [2560,2560] | 35.08 | 77.73 | 0.45× |

Parity passes (max err vs fp64 ref at fp16-accumulation level, 1.7e-6–7.2e-6; BF16→FP16 conversion exact, 0/2,000,000). The warp kernel is already bandwidth-bound at 374 GB/s; the TC path reaches only ~169 GB/s and a single-token GEMV throws away 15/16 of the m16 MMA tile.

Measured on i7-8700K + RTX 2070 8 GB (sm_75, 36 SMs), engine 0.1.27 tree (`bf16_gemv.cu` unchanged through 0.1.30), qwen3.8-flash-next ~125.7B MoE Q2_0 in production. **Conclusions: keep the warp kernel; the benchmark is checked in so nobody has to measure this twice** and can rerun it on future hardware (native bf16, denser GEMV batching). Details and rerun instructions in `bench/results/2026-09-30-tc-gemv-sm75/README.md`.

Limit: latency from back-to-back CUDA-event timing (no ncu profile); production engine ran concurrently on the same GPU.

items.title: decode: hyper-connection read in 2 kernels, stream-split (-1.5 ms per verify window)
items.body:
## Summary

In `fused_gr_read_multi` the norm kernel ran on only T blocks (~16 us of pure latency per call, 96 calls per verify
window) and `down` on 41 blocks (~280 GB/s). v3 does the hyper-connection read in 2 kernels instead of 3:

- `down` is split over (row group, stream) = 164 blocks; each block stages its stream's R' * w_norm for the T tokens,
  reduces that stream's sum of squares itself, and writes UNSCALED per-stream partial dots
- since the rms scale is per stream, w_down . xn = sum_c rs[c] * (w_down[:, c] . (R'[c] * w_norm[c])), and `up`
  applies it in its prologue (lo, inject, rs)

One commit on top of 0.1.27 (a790805); all four of my current branches were compile-tested together on 0.1.27.

## Measured

Measured on 2x RTX 3090, IQ3_S, with the engine this was developed in (0.1.24 + the dual-GPU work): decode verify
window 23.25 -> 21.69 ms (about +7 % decode).

## Correctness

Same maths, another summation order, so NOT bitwise identical to the old kernels. Our dual-vs-single exactness gate
passes with it (both paths use it).

## Switches

`STRATA_GR_V3=0` = the old 3 kernels. A/B knobs measured neutral or slower, left off by default:
`STRATA_GR_KSPLIT=2`, `STRATA_GR_DOWN_R2=2`, `STRATA_GR_UP_PF=1`.

items.body:
## Title
<!-- If Applicable, reference the GitHub issue -->
Issue: Related context: #1349 and #1910; no issue resolution is claimed.

Opt-in persistent cache for immutable BF16-to-FP16 prompt weights

## Summary
<!-- Quick Summary of changes -->
Avoid repeated conversion of explicitly immutable BF16 weights on the active CUDA FP16 BF16_TC path.
Rebased onto `origin/main` pinned at `a0116b2782a5b82622358c04a06496485d12b2d6`.
Current head: `a9274aaaa2423de9c94b61d8d171041fcf7c1b16`.
This is independent of other optimization PRs. The existing default is unchanged.

## What changed
<!-- Specifics on files changed, and what changes were made there -->
- `include/strata/prefill/gemm.hpp`, `src/prefill/gemm.cu`: explicit `bf16_immutable` API,
  invalidation, statistics and a bounded persistent per-owner conversion arena. Entries use source pointer
  and weight shape on the owner's device; first-admitted entries remain until invalidation/destruction.
  Full/oversize misses convert per call without evicting retained weights.
- Preserve newer upstream HIP/hipBLASLt, strided GEMM APIs, CUDA FP16 algorithm retry and Pascal/FP16
  low-memory tiling rather than restoring the old implementation. Cached and uncached FP16 activation
  conversion respects padded input rows; add a focused packed-versus-strided regression case.
- `include/strata/prefill/prefill.hpp`, `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: expose persistent reserve pricing and
  opt resident immutable model weights into caching. Mutable dequantization scratch, activations and
  drafter weights are not cached. Preserve newer source-dependent prefill sizing.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: reserve the persistent arena independently of loans in skip-if-fits,
  stage room, automatic/adaptive reserves, explicit/native cache caps, post-writeback and owned-fit checks.
  `owned_prefill_mib()` includes the cache even when buffers are borrowed, alongside estimated/exact
  owned buffers otherwise. Callers inherit the price without adding it again, including a separately
  merged peer-capacity PR. No peer planner or peer-specific header/API is added.
  The post-writeback reserve is initialized before the allocation loop via `cache_writeback_reserve`;
  the independent peer PR shares that baseline extraction and replaces the reserve with its full
  pending-allocation holdback. Non-peer persistence is preserved, while peer persistence is counted
  once through `owned_prefill_mib()` rather than added again.
- `src/prefill/gemm_bf16_parity.cu`, `CMakeLists.txt`: configuration parsing, reuse, mutable bypass,
  shape keys, budget fallback/retention, invalidate/pointer reuse, separate streams, prompt-shape parity,
  inactive reservations and strided input checks. Keep default cuBLAS parity.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: configuration, lifetime, pricing and explicitly historical throughput-neutral evidence.

Only exact `STRATA_BF16_TC_CACHE=1` enables the cache. `STRATA_BF16_TC_CACHE_MIB` defaults to 256 MiB per
`Gemm`, accepts 1..65536 MiB, and disables caching with a diagnostic for invalid values. The arena exists
only on the active FP16 BF16_TC path: CUDA Volta by default and Turing with `STRATA_BF16_TC=1`;
not an RTX 8000 name gate. Native BF16, Pascal FP32 and HIP reserve no arena.
`STRATA_BF16_TC=2` is only the tests' forced FP16 mode.

Each owner has one model lifetime, device and fixed stream, with host-serialized calls. The immutable
source stays allocated and unchanged until invalidation/destruction. Invalidate before mutation, unload
or pointer reuse; invalidation waits for the stream and reuses the arena. Cross-stream uploads require
explicit ordering. The arena is never a loan and competes with expert VRAM. BF16_TC rounding remains
unchanged, not a guarantee of native-BF16 bit identity or cross-library determinism.

items.title: sm_75: run the prompt path's BF16 products on the FP16 tensor cores (+15-18 % prefill on RTX 2080 Ti)
items.body:
## What

Turing (sm_75) and Volta (sm_70) have FP16 tensor cores but no BF16 ones, so `cublasGemmEx` on `CUDA_R_16BF` inputs falls back to a SIMT fp32 kernel (`magma_sgemmEx`). On an RTX 2080 Ti that was the largest kernel of the prompt path, **20 % of a 4K prompt** (nsys). It runs every `Gemm::bf16` product: the hyper-connection down / up projections, the router and indexer rows, and PLE key / value.

On compute capability 7.x, `Gemm::bf16` now:
- converts the weight and the activations BF16 → FP16, the activations in row slices of at most 32 MiB;
- runs the existing `Gemm::f16` product (fp32 accumulate) on the tensor cores.

BF16 → FP16 is exact for every value inside FP16's range, because the 7-bit mantissa fits in 10 bits.

- **Scope.** Only compute capability 7.x (Volta, Turing) by default; every other card runs exactly what it ran before. HIP is untouched (`#if !defined(__HIPCC__)`).
- **Override.** `STRATA_BF16_TC=0/1` forces the path off or on.
- **Single-row products** (N = 1) stay on cuBLAS's GEMV, which is faster than the conversions.
- **Scratch.** It belongs to the `Gemm` instance (there is one, in `Prefill::Impl`) and is freed with it. With Qwen3.8-Flash-Next it peaks at about 45 MiB: the 2560×2560 PLE value weight plus one activation slice.
- **Allocation failure.** If the scratch allocation fails, the call falls back to the cuBLAS BF16 path.

## Accuracy

**New test `gemm_bf16_parity`.** It compares `Gemm::bf16` with cuBLAS's own BF16 product on the same inputs. GPU, synthetic, no model; `--bench` adds timings. It covers:
- the prompt path's shapes;
- a T large enough to slice the activations;
- `beta = 1` accumulation (the bf16x2 low parts);
- an output row stride wider than N.

On the 2080 Ti the worst relative difference is 1.7e-5. With `STRATA_BF16_TC=0` it is 0, so the test also passes unchanged on other cards.

**Real products.** I also checked every `beta = 0` product of a real 32K prompt (400 products) against the cuBLAS BF16 result, with a temporary diagnostic that is not in this PR:
- worst relative difference 3.5e-5;
- no activation outside FP16 range (max |X| 75.5);
- no non-finite values.

**Greedy output.** It matches the unpatched engine for the first 52 (4K) and 105 (32K) tokens, then diverges the usual way for a change in summation order.

`gr_parity` still passes.

## Numbers

Setup:
- RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (PCIe 3.0 x16), i7-6700, 32 GB DDR4-2133, Linux.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0, `--resident-experts`, `--spec 4`.
- Fixed-token prompts, greedy, same binary with `STRATA_BF16_TC=0` vs `1`.

| prompt | prefill t/s, before | after | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4K | 877 | 1020 | +16 % |
| 16K | 1134 | 1337 | +18 % |
| 32K | 1153 | 1366 | +18 % |
| 64K | 1116 | 1312 | +18 % |
| 128K | 1009 | 1166 | +15 % |

Decode does not use `Gemm::bf16` and is unchanged within noise.

Per product (`gemm_bf16_parity --bench`):

| product | cuBLAS BF16 | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| hc down, T 4096 × N 320 × K 10240 | 4428 µs | 1668 µs |
| hc up, T 4096 × N 10240 × K 320 | 3468 µs | 613 µs |
| PLE value, T 777 × N 2560 × K 2560 | 1440 µs | 325 µs |

After the change, the conversion kernel is 3.8 % of a 32K prefill. Writing FP16 directly from the producers would take that back, but it touches more code, so I left it out of this PR.

Measured on sm_75 only (Volta was added in review, unmeasured). Other cards keep the default off, so their path is the same code as before.

items.title: fix(mtp): --batch-mtp exits on the first admission with a draft-vocab head (slot drafters never copy its type)
items.body:
On 0.1.40 (`1735d64`), `--batch 2 --batch-mtp` with an MTP directory that ships `draft_vocab.bin` exits on the first
request that a batch slot takes:

```
strata batch: MTP admission for slot 0 failed: mtp: unsupported native MMVQ GGML type
```

The engine returns 1 and the server reports "the engine stopped unexpectedly". `--batch 2` without `--batch-mtp` runs
fine on the same setup.

**Cause.** In `MtpDrafter::bind` (`src/core/mtp.cpp`) a slot drafter that shares the main drafter's head copies
`dhead_`, `dvocab_` and `n_dvocab_`, but not `dhead_type_`. That stays at its default `-1`, so the first
`native_mmvq(sub ? dhead_type_ : ..., ...)` in `draft_first` hits the `default:` case and throws. Any draft-vocab
subset triggers this, the `--mtp-q4` Q4_0 head included.

**Fix (one line):**

```cpp
        dhead_ = shared->dhead_;
        dhead_type_ = shared->dhead_type_;
        dvocab_ = shared->dvocab_;
        n_dvocab_ = shared->n_dvocab_;
```

**Setup:** RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75, our Turing fork on top of 0.1.40), Windows, CUDA 12.6,
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, MTP draft with `draft_vocab.bin` (48,542 tokens), `--spec 4`, two concurrent
Claude Code agents (each with a ~40K-token prompt).

**Verified** with the fix: the same setup starts, two concurrent requests both finish (batch windows average 3.44
rows, i.e. both slots with their MTP proposals, no exit). Without the
fix the first admission exits every time.
